clue.text: Father almost finishes ploughing in each farmstead

indicators.note: the shortened father comes at the end, finishing off the churned letters
ploughing turns over and churns up soil, so the words in and each are churned into a new order
almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: dad is an everyday word for father

explanation.surface: Dad has nearly done ploughing every field on the ranch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ploughing' turns IN and EACH into HACIEN; DAD less its last letter ('almost') gives DA, which 'finishes' the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A hacienda is a large estate or farmhouse in Spanish-speaking countries, a kind of farmstead.

clue.text: Denunciation of what Washington admitted?

parts.note: a savage attack in words, punning on the tale of young George Washington confessing to cutting down a cherry tree with his tool

explanation.definitionFit: A vicious verbal or written attack is called this; literally it is the work done with a small axe.

clue.text: Success, nothing less, gets you a trophy

indicators.note: less signals that the letter for nothing is removed

parts.note: a coup is a notable successful stroke
o, the round zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: Winning without a loss earns you a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: A cup is a common sporting trophy, often a silver goblet with handles.

clue.text: Charm? Regret accepting love with bloke after upset

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the whole assembled word is turned around in this down clue
accepting says the regret word takes the love and the bloke inside it

parts.note: to rue something is to regret it
love means zero in tennis, written O
a bloke is British slang for a man

explanation.surface: Asks whether someone is charming, then regrets falling for a man after a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'after upset' turns the whole built word bottom to top; 'Charm?' is a verb here, to captivate.
explanation.definitionFit: To enamour someone is to captivate or charm them into love.

clue.text: One makes a change here before going on to a later stage

definitions.text: One makes a change here before going on to a later stage

parts.words: One makes a change here before going on to a later stage
parts.note: reads like a career move, but it is an actor changing costume before going out onto the stage

explanation.definitionFit: A backstage room where performers put on costumes and make-up before their entrance.

clue.text: Is section of animation able to stop?

parts.note: to be able is to be capable, as in 'I can'
a cel is one transparent celluloid sheet in a hand-drawn animated film

explanation.surface: Asks whether one frame of a cartoon can halt.
explanation.definitionFit: To cancel something is to call it off, bringing it to a stop: a direct synonym.

clue.text: Greed? Here's a change, with : no yen to get diamonds

indicators.note: no yen means the letter for yen is removed

parts.note: to vary is to change
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese yen
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: Greed is a novelty when you have no desire for jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: VARY loses its Y for 'no yen', a pun as yen is also a craving.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice is an extreme desire for wealth, a synonym of greed.

clue.text: Supporter has a monopoly on style

parts.note: to corner a market is to gain a monopoly of it
tone is a manner or style

explanation.surface: A fan dominates fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: A cornerstone is the foundation stone supporting a structure, figuratively a vital supporter.

clue.text: Prison dropping first section of chain

indicators.note: dropping first means the opening letter of the prison word goes

parts.note: the clink is slang for a prison

explanation.surface: A jail lets go of the first part of a chain gang.
explanation.definitionFit: A link is one ring or loop forming part of a chain.

clue.text: Wet a part, having turned this on?

definitions.text: Wet a part, having turned this on?

indicators.note: turned signals the letters of these words being turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: You get part of yourself wet after turning on a faucet.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: turn on the kitchen supply and you wet a part of yourself.
explanation.definitionFit: Water from the mains comes out when you turn the faucet, wetting whatever is underneath it.

clue.text: Old woman almost stepped into fellow's embrace

indicators.note: into says the shortened stepping word goes inside the fellow
a fellow's embrace holds something within his arms, so the letters sit inside

parts.note: a man is a fellow

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: trod is the past tense of tread, to step

explanation.surface: An elderly lady nearly walked into a man's arms.
explanation.walkthrough: TROD loses its last letter ('almost') to give TRO, which goes 'into' MAN's 'embrace'.
explanation.definitionFit: A matron is a dignified older married woman; in hospitals and schools the senior woman in charge.

clue.text: Scrub poem

definitions.meaning: scrub as a noun is land covered in stunted bushes, a barren tract

explanation.surface: Clean a verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrubland is waste land; Eliot's celebrated poem bears the same three-word title.

clue.text: It ensures you always get the best of what's on offer

definitions.text: It ensures you always get the best of what's on offer

parts.words: It ensures you always get the best of what's on offer
parts.note: ironic: when only one thing is offered, what you get is by definition the best of the offer

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a free choice that is no choice at all, as only one option is available, so that one is the best.

clue.text: Rather brusque book notice's toned down

parts.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement, here with 's for is
tempered means moderated or toned down

explanation.surface: A review that is somewhat curt has been softened.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone irritable and short with others is curt or brusque in manner.

clue.text: Stupid mistake why, old boy?

indicators.note: something stupid is muddled, so the letters of these words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone asks a former pupil why he made a silly error.
explanation.walkthrough: A WYKEHAMIST is a pupil or former pupil of Winchester College, an old English public school; 'old boy' means a former pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: Old boys of Winchester College are named after its founder, William of Wykeham.

clue.text: Died in defeat that's brought back regal dynasty

indicators.note: in says the abbreviation for died sits inside the other piece
brought back means the word for defeat is read backwards

parts.note: a rout is a crushing defeat
d. is the standard abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: Someone died during a defeat that restored a royal house.
explanation.walkthrough: ROUT 'brought back' gives TUOR, and D goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudors were the royal family ruling England from 1485 to 1603, a regal dynasty.

clue.text: Recently-purchased clothing is in a state

parts.note: something just bought is new
a jersey is a knitted pullover, an item of clothing

explanation.surface: A newly bought outfit is in good condition.
explanation.definitionFit: New Jersey is one of the fifty United States, on the east coast.

clue.text: Attempts at seduction -obvious, sure to fail?

parts.note: overt means open and obvious

indicators.note: if sure fails it falls apart, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asks whether blatant advances are bound to be rejected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to fail' is the anagram signal on sure (giving URES); the surface asks if blatant advances will flop.
explanation.definitionFit: Overtures are opening approaches or advances, and romantic ones are attempts at seduction.

clue.text: Kitchen item to work, holding in first hint of flavour

indicators.note: holding says the work word surrounds the other letters

parts.note: toil is hard work

indicators.note: first hint of picks the opening letter of flavour

explanation.surface: A cooking aid helps keep in the taste.
explanation.walkthrough: TOIL 'holding' IN plus F gives T-INF-OIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinfoil is thin metal sheeting used in kitchens to wrap and cook food.

clue.text: Attend to fire in the city

definitions.meaning: to tend a fire by adding fuel and stirring it
...-on-Trent is a city in Staffordshire, England, known for pottery

explanation.surface: Tending a blaze somewhere in town.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoking a fire keeps it burning; Stoke is the common short name of an English pottery city.

clue.text: Mark article about male perseverance

indicators.note: about means the mark word goes around the male letter

parts.note: a stain is a mark
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An essay on a man's persistence leaves a blemish.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamina is staying power, the ability to persevere through effort.

clue.text: President's first problem, trapped by devious American source of pictures

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the word President's
trapped by says the problem is enclosed within the rearranged letters
devious means winding and indirect, so the letters of American take a twisted order

parts.note: being in a hole is being in trouble, so a hole is a problem

explanation.surface: A president's first difficulty is being snared by a scheming American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devious' gives the anagram INCAMERA; 'trapped by' puts the problem inside it, after the president's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinhole camera is a lensless box that forms images through a tiny hole, a simple source of photographs.

clue.text: A Dalmatian's first to be removed from dog event

indicators.note: removed from says these letters are taken out of the dog word

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them, to shadow

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of Dalmatian's

explanation.surface: A spotted dog's lead entry is withdrawn from a canine contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dog' is a verb: SHADOW less A and D leaves SHOW.
explanation.definitionFit: A show is a public event or exhibition, as a dog show.

clue.text: School headmaster's first to get the point

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of headmaster's

parts.note: an arrow is a pointer, the sign that points the way

explanation.surface: The head of a school is the first to grasp the point.
explanation.walkthrough: HARROW is a famous English public (private boarding) school.
explanation.definitionFit: Harrow School in north-west London is one of the best-known independent schools in England.

clue.text: Girl beginning to cheer, greeting street musicians?

parts.note: Maria is a girl's name

indicators.note: beginning to picks the first letter of cheer

parts.note: hi is a casual greeting

explanation.surface: A girl starts cheering and waves hello to buskers.
explanation.definitionFit: Mariachi are Mexican folk bands who often play in streets and plazas; the question mark admits not all are street players.

clue.text: Character '-Doric speech ultimately has one

indicators.note: ultimately picks the final letters of Doric and speech

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A rustic Scots dialect finally has a personality.
explanation.walkthrough: Doric is a broad Scots dialect.
explanation.definitionFit: Chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet, and a letter is a character.

clue.text: No time for nonsense — get moving, if somewhat slowly

indicators.note: no time means the letter for time is taken away

parts.note: twaddle is silly talk, nonsense

explanation.surface: Stop talking rubbish and get going, even at a slow pace.
explanation.definitionFit: To waddle is to walk with short swaying steps, moving along but rather slowly.

clue.text: Hopeful type with the thought and the inclination

parts.note: an idea is a thought
a list is a lean or tilt, as of a ship, an inclination

explanation.surface: An optimist with both the notion and the desire.
explanation.definitionFit: An idealist pursues high ideals and hopes for perfection, a hopeful type of person.
